summary: Observation of a probable atmospheric reentry
description: On December 31, 1995, at approximately 7:40 PM, a witness driving a car observed a bright green ball with a trail, moving very quickly across the sky, for two to three seconds. The witness's description suggests it was likely an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observations of the silent evolutions of a round object rotating on itself and making back and forth movements: probable observation of a sky-rose (laser animation).
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within an investigation report. This case, previously classified as D and named SAINT-GERMAIN EN LAYE (78) 1995, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On Saturday, December 23, 1995, around 2:00 AM, a witness and a friend observed a huge, round, saucer-shaped object slowly rotating and moving back and forth over a house before settling over a field. The witnesses observed lights all around it. No noise was heard during the observation. The witness, frightened, went home and looked out a window, but the object had disappeared. Only one witness statement was recorded. The UFO observed by the witness was probably just a laser from a local nightclub (also known as a sky tracker) projecting its beams onto the low cloud layer (present that day); see the investigation report. The description of the phenomenon: the witness described a round, enormous shape... not very high above the ground... below this object, we could see lights all around it. It was slowly rotating, moving back and forth, and was above a house. Then it moved closer to me and stabilized above a field... it made no noise. This description is characteristic of the appearance and behavior of a sky tracker, as the lasers can rotate, spin in a circular motion, move back and forth, and stop. The laser beams are not always visible. This depends on the concentration of suspended particles in the atmosphere between the ground and the cloud base. These particles can include water droplets, dust, pollen, pollutants, etc. No information on this subject is available for the period in question. Regarding the location: the witness indicated a house in a place called "L'Arlequin" to the northwest of their position as facing the phenomenon. However, just a few degrees away and slightly further from this place called "L'Arlequin," there is a nightclub, which could have used a sky tracker (which already existed in 1995). The existence of this nightclub is documented as early as 1993. The observation took place on a weekend night, when nightclubs are most active. The conditions allowing the visualization of beam impacts are quite specific, including the type of atmosphere, clouds, and ambient lighting. A single nightclub can create its effects in distinct locations within a 10 to 20 km radius. The GEIPAN database (www.geipan.fr) contains similar cases (search for cases using the keywords "Sky-Tracer" and "Sky Rose laser"). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: Sky Rose.

summary: Observation of a luminous sphere
description: On December 1, 1995, at approximately 7:30 PM, a witness observed a luminous sphere from his home. The sphere descended slowly above his roof and, after a brief pause, moved off again at a slow speed. The witness's testimony was prompted by a radio program about extraterrestrials that asked for any witnesses to come forward. No other information was gathered.

summary: Observation of a halo effect likely originating from a nightclub laser.
description: On November 28, 1995, two witnesses observed a white, luminous ring rotating clockwise in the sky around 6:30 a.m. The previous evening, two municipal police officers had made the same observation around 11:00 p.m. The phenomenon was silent. This ring likely originated from a laser projector at a nightclub.

summary: Observation of 8 luminous spheres arranged in a circle, motionless
description: On November 28, 1995, at approximately 5:00 a.m., a witness leaving for work observed eight luminous orange spheres arranged in a circle. These spheres moved silently and were also seen by another witness despite the thick fog surrounding them. Both witnesses were able to observe the phenomenon for about 10 minutes before leaving for work. No further information has been gathered about this phenomenon.

summary: Observation of a luminous nebula mass with aligned squares: lack of information.
description: On November 25, 1995, at approximately 8:45 PM, a witness driving on the highway observed a faintly luminous nebula for about 20 kilometers, within which aligned rectangles could be distinguished. No further information could be gathered. The case is classified as Class C due to lack of information.

summary: Observation of an advertising projector
description: On November 18, 1995, at approximately 7:00 PM, a witness observed large luminous circles rotating in the sky. An investigation revealed that a nearby Opel dealership had used a laser advertising projector during a promotional campaign. A test, conducted at the request of investigators, confirmed the witness's observation.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On November 16, 1995, at approximately 5:45 PM, a witness observed, for a fleeting duration of 2 to 3 seconds, a very bright white sphere followed by a red trail before disappearing. This observation was likely that of an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On October 15, 1995, at approximately 6:30 PM, two witnesses located at different points observed a luminous sphere with a trail, which appeared to be falling, for a few seconds. No sound was heard, suggesting it was likely an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of a luminous cylinder
description: On October 1, 1995, at approximately 2:45 a.m., a witness in his car observed a cylindrical, aluminum-colored object. For about a minute, he saw a bright orange light coming from a cylinder approximately one meter in diameter. No noise was heard. No other information was collected.

summary: Observation of two luminous red and green balls
description: On September 25th, at approximately 9 PM, two witnesses observed two red-green spheres moving across the sky from their homes. One of the spheres would occasionally rotate around the other. The phenomenon remained silent, and the estimated diameter of the spheres was around 4 or 5 meters. The investigation led to the discovery of another witness who came forward later. No further information could be gathered.

summary: observation of luminous phenomena rotating in the sky
description: On September 12, 1995, at approximately 6:30 a.m., several independent witnesses observed a series of white lights rotating in the sky, sometimes appearing to follow the witnesses' vehicles. The phenomenon remained silent and was observed for about ten minutes. Although all investigations into the matter have been unsuccessful, the witnesses' descriptions are consistent with those generally given when observing laser advertising projectors. It is possible that tests were being conducted in the vicinity at that time.

summary: Observation of bright points in the sky.
description: On September 4, 1995, between 11:00 PM and 2:00 AM, a witness observed several bright points in the sky that appeared to grow larger. The witness observed the movement of numerous bright points in the area of observation. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a probable atmospheric reentry
description: On July 24th at approximately 10:30 PM, a witness observed a very bright, luminous sphere with a trail. The observation was completely silent and lasted about 3 seconds. The witness's description suggests a probable atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of several rapidly moving lights
description: On the night of May 31st to June 1st, 1995, two witnesses observed lights, one for 2 to 3 seconds while driving his car, the other for about ten minutes from his home. Both witnesses reported that these lights moved silently at high speed. Very little information is available about this sighting, preventing any serious analysis.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On June 25, 1995, gendarmes on night patrol observed, around 11:45 p.m., the very rapid passage of a very bright luminous sphere before it disappeared. The gendarmes likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Likely sighting of a disco projector
description: On April 30, 1995, at approximately 3:30 a.m., a witness and his wife observed a bright, luminous mass with numerous bright points moving across the sky. The investigation quickly revealed that it was likely a "Sky Rose" disco spotlight, the light of which is visible from several kilometers away depending on cloud cover and atmospheric conditions.

summary: Observation of a luminous shape in the sky
description: On May 29, 1995, around 1:00 a.m., a couple in a car observed a luminous, oval-shaped object in the sky. Beams of light emanated from this object, and the witnesses felt as if they were being followed. Despite the witnesses' denials, the description of the observed phenomenon strongly suggested a disco spotlight, as the gendarmes of that brigade had received numerous reports of similar sightings. The effects produced by these types of devices do indeed vary depending on weather conditions and the distance from which they are observed.

summary: Observation of a very bright, egg-shaped object, stationary and silent near the ground: lack of information.
description: This sighting, formerly known as LORGUES (83) 14.05.1995, is classified as a D case by SEPRA and is currently under review (see the Investigation Notes document). On May 14, 1995, a witness, alone in an isolated campsite, spotted a luminous, egg-shaped UFO between the trees, but close to him. The object was silent and stationary, about 1 meter above the ground. The witness attempted to photograph it, but the camera malfunctioned. The UFO then appeared to change size and move towards the witness, who became frightened and ran away to call the police. He returned to his tent in their presence. During the investigation, the police found no traces on the ground or in the vegetation, and no other witness statements were collected. No military aircraft were reported to have been flown over the area on the evening of the sighting. This case is inconsistent (a single, isolated witness), but the description of the observed UFO is quite precise. The witness's sincerity and credibility have never been questioned. However, the imprecision regarding the timing is a serious obstacle to formally identifying the UFO. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (direction of observation, shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: the Moon. The issue is not the witness's visual perception, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their feelings (panic, fatigue, nighttime observation). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak strangeness is classified as C e, meaning it cannot be identified due to a lack of data, although a misidentification with the Moon is considered.

summary: Observation of a large object above a house with supposed effects on witnesses, animals and plants.
description: Between May 25 and 28, 1995, at approximately 3:30 a.m., a couple observed a large, dark object, possibly a helicopter, hovering above their house. The object remained stationary, without any noise, smoke, or trail. After a few minutes, having shone beams of light on the ground five or six times, the object departed at moderate speed. During this observation, the witness's dogs went inside the house without barking. About a week later, the dogs began vomiting and suffering from diarrhea. The witness's wife experienced health problems, while he himself felt extremely fatigued. The witness also noted some vegetation decline in the area where the beams had been illuminated. He also reported the sudden hospitalization of a neighbor. Frightened, he decided to call Civil Security to find out if a link could be established between the observed phenomenon and the effects he noticed on himself, his wife, his neighbor, his dogs, and his plants. The investigation, while failing to identify the observed object, also failed to establish any connection between the object's appearance and the supposed effects. The witnesses' health problems can be explained, on the one hand, by the treatment the witness's wife was undergoing and, on the other hand, by the intense heat. The neighbor's hospitalization is not surprising given his age. Numerous plants located outside the area supposedly affected by the object showed similar signs of decline. Nevertheless, the observed phenomenon remains unexplained.

summary: Observations of a stationary dark mass above a field and its rapid departure and disappearance in the sky: lack of information.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named PELLOUAILLES-LES-VIGNES (49) 24.04.1995, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. This case concerns the observation of a UFO (Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon) by three witnesses on April 24, 1995, around 9:30 PM in a locality within the commune of SAINT-SYLVAIN-D'ANJOU (49). The witnesses were outside when they noticed the presence of a UFO in an uncultivated field. They described a large, oval-shaped mass, gray to concrete-like in color, stationary in the field, between 10 and 15 meters high. No noise was heard, particularly when the UFO moved and disappeared at very high speed in a northeasterly direction. A red light was seen during the brief observation. The witnesses immediately went to the field at the presumed location of the UFO but found nothing unusual. The Gendarmerie was contacted and interviewed the witnesses, and the press published an article the day after the sighting (the article was not included in the official report). The UFO's diffuse appearance in its initial phase, followed by a sharper, more compact, and colored appearance at the end of the observation, along with its behavior consisting of a phase of immobility followed by a phase of rapid movement, supports the hypothesis of confusion with the impact of a mobile nightclub spotlight on the lower cloud layer (see the investigation report). This impact would have been observed by witnesses initially far from its source, then, as the spotlight was oriented more vertically at the end of the observation, further from the witnesses but closer to the source. This explains the reduction in size, the less flattened shape, the increased brightness, and the sharper color (that of the source) as the beam approaches the vertical. These laser-type projectors (also commonly called "skytrackers") were widely used for advertising purposes, often by nightclubs in the 1980s and 90s. GEIPAN (the French National Group for the Study of Explosive Orbital Projects) has recorded numerous sightings resulting from misinterpretations caused by these installations (see www.geipan.fr and search for cases using the keyword "laser"). Furthermore, in the official report, the police officers noted that a newspaper article published the day after the sighting suggested that a laser lighting test had been carried out by a nightclub at the same time as the sighting. This could not be confirmed, as the police did not provide the newspaper article, and the nightclub owner never appeared before the police, despite several summonses. The three witnesses mentioned a small red light, smaller than the main shape, accompanying it. In 1995, red lasers already existed, albeit with more limited power, and therefore range, than today. Skytracers from the 1990s are not lasers, but conventional light projectors. Laser technology allows for finer and brighter beams. This could explain the (localized) impact mark of a laser tested that day, coupled with the conventional projector. However, there is no evidence to support such an explanation. There remains an element of lingering strangeness, as this has never been observed in GEIPAN's laser sightings. The case is weak. Important data is missing, such as azimuth and elevation angle measurements of the UFOs, as well as their angular size. The witnesses did not provide sketches of the UFO, despite requests from the police during the interviews, which somewhat compromises the assessment of the testimonies' reliability. An on-site investigation at the time would have clarified many points, in addition to those mentioned above, and could have either confirmed or ruled out the nightclub experiment hypothesis, if the manager of the nightclub suspected of causing the confusion had been interviewed or visited at the time. We have a plausible hypothesis based on the overall appearance and a potential explanation regarding the original nightclub. However, the red dot noted by witnesses is a peculiar point for this hypothesis and adds a certain degree of residual strangeness. In comparison, the evidence is weak and insufficient to validate a hypothesis with such a significant element of strangeness, and even weaker to establish an unexplained nature if the hypothesis were to be rejected altogether. It is not possible to draw a conclusion. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Observing the passage of a formation of bright points in the sky
description: On March 15, 1995, at approximately 10:30 PM, a witness observed a formation of bright points moving in a straight line across the sky for a few seconds. No further information is available.

summary: Observation of a very bright point of light with a sudden, rapid, candle-like start.
description: On February 22, 1995, at approximately 6:20 a.m., a witness observed a very bright flashing point moving with rapid acceleration, accompanied by a sudden lurch. No further information is available.

summary: Observation by a family of the movement of a bright white light in the sky on a straight trajectory: probable observation from the Mir space station.
description: The GEIPAN publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named BEAUNE (21) 22.02.1995, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On February 22, 1995, after 10:30 p.m., three members of the same family (two adults and a 12-year-old child) were intrigued by a UFO (Unidentified Flying Object) above their home. The witnesses, looking through a skylight, described an object as a star, luminous white. Not all eyewitness accounts agree on the UFO's movement. The observation lasted two to three minutes. The witnesses likely observed a passage of the MIR space station, visible in the sky at the date and time of the observation (see the investigation report). This conclusion is based on the following points: - the witnesses' description of the UFO's shape, color, and size, described as a large, bright white star, is entirely consistent; - the speed described as rather slow by T1 corresponds well with the apparent speed of MIR; - regarding the direction of movement, we were able to show that the MIR station, present in the sky that evening, was indeed moving towards the south-southeast. (T3's mention of immobility could perhaps be explained by the brevity of the beginning of his observation, but above all, there is a contradiction between T3 and the police, who state that T3 did indeed see the UFO moving); - The observation period is mostly reported by witnesses as being short, and in any case not exceeding three minutes, which corresponds perfectly with the duration of the MIR station's pass. (T2's mention of a duration of 15 minutes probably refers to the final phase following the disappearance of the phenomenon; the witness may have continued observing in the hope of seeing the UAP again); - T2's mention of repositioning slightly further from the UAP without observing any movement is entirely consistent with what can be observed for some satellites, so the brightness can fluctuate significantly and rapidly, even giving the impression of a blackout followed by a relighting further away. T2's mention of immobility for approximately 30 seconds requires some specific assumptions to remain consistent with the hypothesis. - Overestimation of duration or confusion between the periods of extinction and the periods of ignition of the UFO, or confusion with a similar nearby object (star) during the periods of extinction of the UFO. The failure of other witnesses to mention this immobility in sequences is an element supporting this type of error and confusion by T2. The limiting nature of these latter explanations affects the probability of the MIR hypothesis without invalidating it, given the strength of the other points in favor. The consistency of this case is mediocre: - in terms of information, there remains a great deal of very imprecise or even contradictory data between the testimonies. We can also regret the absence of angular measurements (size, height above the horizon) as well as a precise and detailed chronology of events for each witness; The contradictions undermine the perceived reliability of the testimonies, especially in a context where the first witness, a child (T3), who was aware of the concept of UFOs (through a school lesson that same day) and was looking for a UFO that evening, could have created a strong sense of unease in his parents (T1 and T2) by alerting them, potentially impairing their observational skills or critical thinking. The level of consistency remains sufficient to support the MIR hypothesis, given its high probability. Faced with a greater degree of final strangeness (absence of a hypothesis or a lower probability for the MIR hypothesis), this consistency would have been insufficient to reach a conclusion, and the case would have been classified as C (unusable) and in no case maintained as D (unexplained). See GEIPAN classification methodology. The case is classified as B: probable observation of the MIR space station.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On February 6, 1995, at 7:20 PM, a witness on foot observed the trajectory of a point of light that became increasingly incandescent before disappearing and splitting into two red points. The witness's observation was likely that of an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of a bright light above a forest
description: On January 12, 1995, at 10:10 PM, a witness observed a large luminous phenomenon from their home, seemingly emerging from the woods. This phenomenon illuminated the woods. No sound was heard, and the observation lasted two to three minutes. No further information is available regarding this sighting.
